claim: Portfolio overlap transmits forced-selling shocks and comovement across commonly held assets
The standard holdings-based horizon measure (Gaspar-Massa-Matos churn) nets out passive price changes
Peer effects exist in what institutional fund managers hold and trade (social ties, geography, shared employers)
Short-horizon institutional ownership is associated with more selling in turmoil, higher volatility and crash risk (level effects)
Credible peer-effect estimates need exogenous variation beyond regressing outcomes on peers' mean outcomes
